doc.title: Dick Griffin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 12, 2024

title: Rahsaan Roland Kirk's personality and intelligence
summary: Griffin says he treated Kirk as if he could see, and describes his high IQ, memory and record collecting.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: have a look at that. And then we had this little inside thing. He had a way of rocking. And I said, “Rahsaan, don’t go to that poor blind man move on me.” And he would just laugh and say, “No, man, you pay me this amount of money” and everything. But he would say, “Dick, you know man, if I could see” and he started groaning. I said, “Uh uh, don’t go there, poor blind man, don’t pull that one on me, it ain’t going to work with me today you know. And we would just have so much fun you know and laughing. He loved — because I wouldn’t treat him like he was blind. He was smart. I’ll tell you another thing about Rahsaan, he was probably the person that had the highest IQ of I’ve ever met. He could spell any word that you would – I would tell him to spell, he was very bright, very high IQ. And his friends were, one of his blind friends was a psychiatrist, and he was just smart. And then he never, if you met him one time he’d never didn’t forget you or your name. And he always identified you by your record. He’d come in, I’d introduce him, “This is Dante.” Yeah man, I heard you’ve got this record, you’ve got this record and this one and ba-ba. So he was a really smart guy collecting records and even the cassettes which were just kind of creeping in during the time I was with him.
